body.statement: Can one construct \(\mathsf H_n\) from def:hybrid-handle and derive data-dependent switching thresholds such that one data-dependent confidence procedure has the uniform coverage guarantee of lem:uniform-primitive-inversion over exact-zero, \(n^{-1/2}\)-weak, branch-tie, and basis-tie sequences, while at every fixed regular law satisfying the strict-cell conditions of thm:pointwise-regular-cell-oracle-recovery its endpoints differ from \(\mathcal I_{q,n}^{\mathrm{or}}\) by \(o_p(n^{-1/2})\)?
body.justification: Uniform validity alone can be conservative; the unresolved theorem is whether one procedure can also recover oracle precision whenever the singularities are separated.
body.gap: HongLi2018 gives numerical-delta inference for directional maps, and AndrewsMikusheva2016 combines weak-identification validity with strong-identification efficiency in Gaussian moments, but neither covers a data-dependent transition for a discontinuous supershort-calibrated union of LP values.
body.consumer: Software can default to a single honest procedure rather than forcing practitioners to choose ex ante between a wide robust region and a fragile regular approximation.
